analysis.title: FX Daily: Bearish yield curve flattening lifts the dollar
key_insights: The dollar is near the year's highs after October US CPI came in hot for the third month in a row and Fed governor Chris Waller said he could vote for a 50bp hike at the 9 December FOMC. ING expects the dollar to hold gains on 11 November.

Short-dated Treasury yields rose 20bp and the 2-10 year curve flattened 7bp on Waller's comments and the CPI print. ING says a bearish flattening like this is normally dollar positive and negative for activity currencies, because the Fed is slowing demand.

ING says Waller's 50bp call may be too aggressive for FOMC voters who favour gradual tightening, but it keeps alive the prospect that the Fed needs three more hikes. It describes Fed Chair Kevin Warsh as aiming to slow demand and return inflation to target since his first press conference in June.

The NOK and SEK underperformed in the strong dollar environment on 10 November. ING says the CHF suffers in higher-rate environments this year. ING expects the dollar to hold and test the top of its trading ranges over the coming weeks.

Trading on 11 November should be thin because of the US Veterans Day holiday. October PPI on Friday could add another hot price reading and keep the dollar bid. ING sees DXY retesting resistance at 102.85/103.00.

EUR/USD has a floor at 1.1110, the 50% retracement of the 25 March to 26 Jan rally, which ING says is a reasonable level for speculative accounts to take profits on short EUR/USD. ING thinks the bounce case is weak and expects EUR/USD to press the lower end of a 1.10-1.15 range as a hawkish Fed dominates into year-end.

ING expects the ECB to match a Fed hike in December, with ECB speakers supporting a hike to 2.75% on 17 December. ING says the case for an extended ECB tightening cycle is far weaker than for the Fed.

Reuters Tankan manufacturing sentiment in Japan hit a five-year high, driven by semiconductor and data centre demand. Strong profits and wage growth could feed the BoJ's view that inflation is stable at 2.00% and that accommodative policy can be reined in.
ING says USD/JPY could push through resistance at 159, but investors are likely to buy yen if it moves above 160 again.

Hungarian headline CPI rose to 2.0% in October on fuel prices, with core at 2.1% and no clear second-round effects. ING expects 3.0% inflation in December and a 3.4% average in 2027. It expects the National Bank of Hungary to hold at 5.50% through year-end, with further cuts more likely in the second half of 2027.

Czech headline inflation was confirmed at 2.4% and core stayed at 3.1%, one-tenth below the CNB forecast. ING expects headline inflation near 3% in December and near 4% in January and February, then a decline. It sees risks to the upside and says an upside surprise would lead to more tightening after the CNB's November hike.

In CEE rates, early moves lower on falling energy prices reversed after US CPI. ING says oil has fallen sharply but gas has not, and gas matters more to CEE ahead of winter. It keeps its view of higher EUR-cross pairs in CEE.
